upright.basis: User-presented natural upright pose. No independent gravity-vertical instrument is recorded.

frozen_lag.objective: First AUTO trial only; modes2/3; 0.3<=|firmware omega|<=20; residual centered per lag, largest5% removed.
frozen_lag.convention: Compare camera at source t to encoder at mapped host t+lag. A negative lag means camera corresponds to earlier encoder data.
frozen_lag.limitation: Descriptive timing alignment, not exposure-latency calibration. Support range is not a confidence interval.

conclusions.evidence: A frozen constant+lag leaves several degrees of discrepancy. First-trial angle features reduce RMS on later trials more consistently than a residual rate or direction term; this supports repeatable angle-associated disagreement in these trajectories.
conclusions.scope: The evidence identifies sensor-pair disagreement, not which sensor is wrong. Camera projection/marker geometry, view changes, timing jitter, coupling/loading, and magnetic encoder response remain possible contributors.
conclusions.static_caution: Camera framing moved before the new upright check. Its camera anchor is never applied to old520 images. Cross-frame up/down angular comparisons are unavailable.
conclusions.operational: Saving a measured upright can correct its zero. It cannot by itself establish accuracy away from upright or prove balance performance.

method.anchor: Original520 cohort retains its saved encoder zero and raw image vertical; no new upright anchoring is applied. Later upright summary is independent context only. Raw camera is derived from marker geometry; no fusion or saved camera calibration.
method.models: OLS on first native AUTO trial only, coefficients frozen on later trials; circular residuals kept on their small-error branch. No parameter or firmware calibration is emitted.
method.uncertainty: Frames are temporally correlated and pose/speed/cart state are not independently varied. No formal confidence interval or systematic nonlinear calibration validation.
method.provenance: Prior source hashes are retained in the linked base report; this manifest hashes that report, its paired data, upright raw sources, and both scripts.
